content: 1. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of clonazepam by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of CYP3A4. When co-administered with CYP3A substrates, their levels should be monitored, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 3. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of clorazepate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elagolix by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is required. 5. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended due to potential interactions. 6. Combining elagolix (a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer) with cobicistat (a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate) may increase elagolix levels and decrease cobicistat levels. Refer to prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 7. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of cobimetinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 8. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of cocaine topical by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 9.
